title: 128k context probes: truncation & attention-sink tests
content:
Working notes: 128k context probes — truncation & attention sink tests

Purpose:
- Rapidly validate model behavior & runtime stability for very long contexts (8k, 32k, 128k) with retrieval-style prompts.
- Exercise truncation logic, prefix-preservation, KV-cache pressure, and pathological attention patterns ("attention sinks").
- Surface mitigations we can apply in Redwood Optimize and runtime routing/variants for Dedicated/Private customers.

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: LM A/B on internal onboarding models + two community baselines. Run end-to-end on 1xA100-80GB and 2x80GB cluster for 128k.
- Non-goal: exhaustive SFT/LLM quality; focus on failure modes and operational signals (OOMs, latency spikes, token drop, truncated retrievals).

Hardware / infra used:
- single-node: A100-80GB (dev lab)
- multi-node cluster emulation: 2xA100 (staging cluster)
- runtime: rw-infer v0.9.8 branch (attention-profiling hooks enabled)
- harness: bench-runner v2 (python harness that can stream inserts and TTL retrievals)

Models tested:
- onboarding candidate: rw-rlhf-1-8k (baseline)
- long-window variant: rw-rlhf-1-32k
- experimental 128k-variant: rw-rlhf-1-128k-fp16q (quantized test build)
- open baseline: longformer-like-community-32k (for comparison)

Prompt sets and retrieval scaffolding (short descriptions):
- Retrieval-sim-small: 50 examples, each with 1 top-10 retrieved doc up to 4k tokens, prompt = user question + concatenated retrieved doc(s). Designed to test truncation when doc appended after prompt.
- Retrieval-sim-large: 30 examples, each with 10 retrieved chunks (avg 8k each) — unrealistic but stresses concatenation + attention.
- Cumulative-context-chain: synthetic chain of 64 micro-docs (2k tokens each) appended sequentially; used to stress KV-cache size and attention growth.
- Attention-sink-probes: crafted inputs with repeated cross-references designed to force quadratic attention hotspots (e.g., many repeated entity mentions and repeated tabular cross-links).

Test harness config (not exhaustive):
- tokenization: gpt2-bpe; measure tokens at both prompt assembly and at model input.
- truncation policy: runtime default (truncate from tail of concatenated retrievals when exceeding max_window). Also ran preserve-prefix experiments (preserve user prompt, drop oldest retrieval chunk).
- batching: batch_size=1 for latency-focused runs; batch_size=4 for throughput checks.
- streaming: disabled for these stability runs (makes profiling simpler).

Matrix of runs (representative):
- Run A: 8k window, Retrieval-sim-small, preserve-prefix=false
- Run B: 8k window, Retrieval-sim-small, preserve-prefix=true
- Run C: 32k window, Retrieval-sim-large, preserve-prefix=true
- Run D: 128k window, Cumulative-context-chain, preserve-prefix=true
- Run E: 128k window, Attention-sink-probes, preserve-prefix=true

Key observations (summary):
- 8k: behavior stable. Truncation occurs predictably at ~8176 tokens (consistent with tokenizer accounting for special tokens). Retrieval items at tail often get dropped; preserve-prefix=true significantly improved user-prompt preservation but retrieval recall dropped ~18% (measured by exact-string presence).
- 32k: generally stable for pad-limited inputs. We observed occasional KV-cache pressure causing latency outliers (95p latency +40%) on multi-concurrent runs. No OOMs in single-node runs.
- 128k: highly variable. Two dominant failure modes observed:
  1) Memory blowups / OOMs on naive full-attention runs for Attention-sink-probes when the input had dense cross-references — runtime crashed on ~30% of samples on single A100 80GB.
  2) Severe latency amplification: token generation cost increases super-linearly when large LV-window is populated; average per-token GPU utilization rose but with long GC pauses in runtime (~150-400ms).
- Attention sink specifics: repeated entity references across many chunks generated attention matrices with many near full-rank sub-blocks, leading to peak memory allocations >2x expected for the same token count without repeated references.

Detailed notes per run:
- Run A (8k, small): all 50 examples completed. Average generation latency 220ms/token; 0 crashes. Notes: retrieval tail truncation removed 1–2 supporting facts in 10 cases.

- Run B (8k, preserve-prefix): cost +3% latency; reduced truncation of user prompt to near-0 but retrieval recall drop measured: for QA tasks where answer depends on retrieved evidence after prompt, exact-answer recall dropped 18%. Conclusion: preserve-prefix viable as default for customer-facing interactions where prompt integrity is critical.

- Run C (32k): 30/30 completed single-node. In multi-concurrent (3 concurrent streams) we saw 2 latency outliers correlated with KV-cache rebuild (profile attached in linked artifact). Investigate cache eviction heuristics.

- Run D (128k cumulative): 12/16 completed; 4 OOMs. OOMs correlated with chunk sizes >4k tokens per chunk. Using windowed generation (slice context into 16k windows with retrieval metadata and answer-merge) avoided OOMs but introduced small hallucination rate increase (~4% measured on closed-set QA).

- Run E (128k attention-sink probes): 18/20 crashed on naive full-attention; on quantized fp16q build, 12/20 crashed but with different failure mode (matrix-multiply overflow conversion runtime error in cuBLAS path). Suggest kernel robustness work and fallback kernels.

Failure signal capture (what to log):
- OOM stack + memstats (CUDA free/total at time of failure), attention matrix sizes, token index map (where repeated entities occur), which kernel (cuBLAS/cuSparse/etc.), and model variant tag.
- Always persist a small serialized prefix of the prompt and retrieval ids (not full doc) for repro.

Hypotheses and root causes (working):
- Hypothesis 1: Repeated cross-references create effectively denser attention matrices due to repeated keys, causing intermediate buffers to spike. Suggest structural deduplication at retrieval assembly (hash-based dedupe for near-duplicate spans).
- Hypothesis 2: KV-cache eviction policy (LRU-ish) thrashes when many near-duplicate tokens are present leading to repeated writes; consider workload-aware chunking to reduce cache churn.
- Hypothesis 3: Quantization kernels in fp16q path are not exercising fallback for pathological sparsity patterns — need kernel hardening.

Mitigations tried during runs (short):
- preserve-prefix truncation: keep user prompt intact, drop oldest retrieval chunks first — good UX tradeoff.
- chunk-level dedupe: removed exact-duplicate spans from retrieved set pre-assembly — reduced OOM frequency in 128k runs by ~30%.
- windowed generation (sliding window + meta-postprocess): avoided OOMs entirely but requires answer-merge logic & careful faithfulness checks.
- fallback to safe-kernel (slower cuBLAS path) on detection of attention-sink signature — eliminated crashes but doubled latency for affected requests.

Actionable next steps (prioritized):
1) Engineering: add attention-sink detector in runtime that computes a cheap sketch (e.g., token-frequency entropy + chunk-similarity) and triggers safe-kernel or windowing. (Owner: Marco)
2) Research: build synthetic probe corpus that enumerates degrees of inter-chunk cross-reference to better calibrate detection thresholds. (Owner: Lina)
3) Runtime: implement hashed span dedupe in retrieval assembly with opt-out flag. (Owner: Ethan)
4) Product: update onboarding checklist to recommend preserve-prefix=true for Hosted API customers by default; document tradeoffs. (Owner: Aisha)
5) Ops: add richer crash telemetry (memstats + kernel id + small prompt snapshot) to Sentry hooks. (Owner: SRE team ticket INF-1293)

Open questions / discussion points:
- What is acceptable tradeoff for Hosted default: preserve prompt vs retrieval recall? propose A/B with 100k calls to measure end-to-end UX.
- For Dedicated/private: should we expose an "attention-safety" knob to choose windowing vs kernel-fallback vs allow-crash? Security/regulatory implications if we change retrieval ordering.
- Where to surface these heuristics in Redwood Console? per-model toggle? per-app?

Attachments / repro pointers:
- See linked artifacts above (bench-runner logs + PR). Repro script: scripts/repro/128k_probe_runner.py (GH PR referenced).

Quick TODO (short):
- [ ] Convert dedupe prototype into a feature flag in retrieval-assembly (Ethan)
- [ ] Implement cheap attention-sink detector (Marco)
- [ ] Run A/B on preserve-prefix default for Hosted (product + experiments)
- [ ] Draft customer-facing note for Enterprise onboarding: limitations and best practices for >32k contexts (Aisha)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep runs reproducible: seed random retrieval ranker with fixed seed.
- Save at least 3 crashing examples for post-mortem.
- Follow up with kernel engineering for quantized path.

End of working note.
